newsitem.title: USA: Donnelley Q3 hurt by lower paper prices.
newsitem.headline: Donnelley Q3 hurt by lower paper prices.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co said lower paper prices dragged down third-quarter sales in its print-related businesses.
Quarterly sales were down six percent, or $102 million, to $1.6 billion from the year-ago quarter, the company said.
"Lower paper prices resulted in a $133 million sales decline in the period," the company said, adding that volume gains in most businesses offset declines elsewhere.
Results for Metromail Corp were deconsolidated from Donnelley results after Metromail's second-quarter initial public offering, the company said.

Donnelley had a $44-million pre-tax gain on the Metromail offering in the second quarter. The company's remaining interest in Metromail is being accounted for as an equity investment. Metromail's 1996 net sales and operating earnings were $126 million and $13 million, respectively, through the date of the offering. Results of the two companies were deconsolidated on June 19, Donnelly said.
The company also cited declines in byproduct prices and lower volume in its Stream business in the third quarter.
"We are taking decisive action in a tough environment for our industry," said chief executive John Walter.
The company took a $560-million restructuring charge in the first half.

"The one-time charges and costs associated with our strategic realignment and business restructuring over the first nine months of 1996 have affected current earnings. But they also have embedded cost and asset productivity benefits in our business, which we will realize in 1997," Walter said.
Shares in the publishing giant were off 3/8 to 31-7/8.
"The actions we are taking will strengthen our businesses as we move forward," Walter said.

"Adjusted for declines in by-products sales, our print-related businesses have improved year to year, and these improvements will continue in 1997 as the benefits of our restructurings are achieved," he said.

"Our operating cash flow is strong, despite lower earnings. We are managing our capital and cash flow carefully, using the value we've realized through the Metromail sale to pay down debt and repurchase shares. We also are addressing the issues Stream faces in fast-changing technology markets, continuing the transition away from manufacturing and aggressively reducing fixed costs," Walter said.
